{{Short description|Greek scientist (born 1945)}}

{{BLP primary sources|date=August 2012}}
'''Phaedon Avouris''' ({{langx|el|Φαίδων Αβούρης}}) is a [[Greece|Greek]] [[Chemical physics| chemical physicist]] specializing in nanoscience and [[nanotechnology]]. His research at the [[Thomas J. Watson Research Center|IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center]] focuses on the applications of molecular devices in computing and electronics. This includes experimental and theoretical studies on the electronics and photonics of [[Carbon nanotube|carbon nanotubes]] (CNT) and [[graphene]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=am |first=Adreaana Collis-27/10/2018 10:22 |date=2016-09-19 |title=Manager of Nanoscience and Nanotechnology in IBM - ellines.com |url=https://www.ellines.com/en/famous-greeks/30518-manager-of-nanoscience-and-nanotechnology-in-ibm/ |access-date=2025-06-30 |website=ellines.com - Η πρώτη διαδικτυακή χώρα στον κόσμο}}</ref>

==Biography==
Phaedon Avouris was born in 1945 in [[Athens]], [[Greece]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Phaedon Avouris – NAS |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/phaedon-avouris-slfxhs/ |access-date=2024-11-09 |website=www.nasonline.org |language=en-US}}</ref> In 1968, he received a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] in chemistry from the [[Aristotle University of Thessaloniki|Aristotle University]] in [[Thessaloniki]], Greece. After postdoctoral work at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], he attended [[Michigan State University]] in 1974 and earned a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[physical chemistry]].<ref name=":0" /> Avouris was an [[Adjunct professor|adjunct research professor]] at [[Columbia University]], [[New York (state)|NY]] in 2003<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academia.edu - Find Research Papers, Topics, Researchers |url=https://ibm.academia.edu/Avouris/CurriculumVitae |access-date=2025-02-26 |website=ibm.academia.edu}}</ref> and was appointed an Adjunct Research Professor in the ECE Department at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign]] in 2016.<ref name=":0" />

==Awards and honours==
Avouris is a member of the following academies and societies:

* [[National Academy of Sciences]] (elected 2017)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/phaedon-avouris-slfxhs/|title=Phaedon Avouris|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref>
* [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (elected 2003)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/phaedon-avouris|title=Phaedon Avouris|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|date=13 September 2023 }}</ref>
* [[Academy of Athens (modern)|Academy of Athens]], (corresponding member, elected 2007)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Academy of Athens Member Directory|date=23 November 2015 |url=http://www.academyofathens.gr/en/organization/members/1st-section}}</ref>
* [[IBM Academy of Technology]] (elected 2004)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Phaedon Avouris – NAS |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/phaedon-avouris-slfxhs/ |access-date=2025-03-14 |website=www.nasonline.org |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Academia.edu - Find Research Papers, Topics, Researchers |url=https://ibm.academia.edu/Avouris/CurriculumVitae |access-date=2025-03-14 |website=ibm.academia.edu}}</ref>

He is also a fellow of the:

* [[American Physical Society]] (APS), 1987
* [[Institute of Physics and Engineering in Medicine|Institute of Physics]] (U.K.), 2004
* [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE), 2014
* [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS), 1996
* [[Materials Research Society]] (MRS), 2011
* [[American Vacuum Society]] (AVS), 1997
* [[World Technology Network]], 1999{{Citation needed|date=March 2025}}

Avouris's work has been recognized with awards from scientific institutions, including:

* Irving Langmuir Prize for Chemical Physics, American Physical Society, 2003<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm|title=Prize Recipient|website=www.aps.org}}</ref>
* Medard W. Welch Award for Surface Science, American Vacuum Society, 1997<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://avs.org/awards/professional-awards/medard-w-welch-award/|title=AVS – Medard W Welch Award}}</ref>
* IEEE Nanotechnology Section, [[Pioneer Award in Nanotechnology]], 2010
* Richard Feynman Prize for Nanotechnology, Foresight Institute, 1999<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://foresight.org/about/1999Feynman.html#1999Winners|title=Richard Feynman Prize}}</ref>
* Julius Springer Prize for Applied Physics (with T. Heinz), 2008
* MRS David Turnbull Lectureship, Materials Research Society, 2011<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mrs.org/careers-advancement/awards/fall-awards/david-turnbull-lectureship|title=David Turnbull Lectureship|website=www.mrs.org}}</ref>
* Richard E. Smalley Prize of the Electrochemical Society, 2009
* H. Bloch Medal, Excellence of Research in Industry, Univ. of Chicago, 2015
* IBM Exceptional Achievement Corporate Award, 2011
* Outstanding Technical Achievement Awards, IBM Corporation, 1989, 1993, 2000, 2002, 2003, 2013, 2015
* Honorary Doctorate, International Hellenic University, 2013
* Member of the National Academy of Sciences, 2017<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academia.edu - Find Research Papers, Topics, Researchers |url=https://ibm.academia.edu/Avouris/CurriculumVitae |access-date=2025-03-04 |website=ibm.academia.edu}}</ref>
* Distinguished Alumnus Award, Michigan State University, 2001
